result.title: When Cell Crops Share a Parent: Measuring and Isolating Acquisition Leakage in Cervical Cytology Benchmarks
result.summary: Public cervical cytology benchmarks release many cell crops cut from far fewer microscope fields or slides and are often split at the crop level, so test cells share acquisition parents with training cells. In a preregistered study, crop-level splitting raised SIPaKMeD accuracy by 0.97 percentage points across twelve architectures and twenty seeds (95% CI 0.59-1.39), and CRIC accuracy by 12.08 points (11.16-12.99). On SIPaKMeD, a factorial that fixes training crop and parent counts attributes the gain to sibling exposure (1.73 points, 0.95-2.51), not to the extra parent diversity of crop-level splits (0.00). Parent identity is decodable at about 100 times chance, yet erasing 82% of its above-floor linear recoverability left the gap unchanged, and Grad-CAM did not distinguish leaking from clean models; matching test cells' color statistics to an unseen same-class field removed most of the advantage. Decodability and saliency cannot substitute for a parent-disjoint split.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在宫颈细胞学基准中量化「同一显微镜视野/切片裁出的细胞 crop 被分到训练与测试两侧」造成的采集泄漏：预注册实验显示 crop 级划分使 SIPaKMeD 与 CRIC 准确率虚高，并用因子设计、父本身份探针与线性可恢复性擦除、Grad-CAM 及颜色统计匹配来定位增益来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「线性可解码不等于被模型使用」以及探针—擦除—显著性—混淆匹配的对照诊断，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真正参与答案、视觉旁路与贡献分配问题；领域较远，迁移需自行判断。
